useCases.text: Used Claude Code to build this whole dashboard last night.
Used Chat GPT to select the best ice cream to eat for breakfast today.
Used Claude to create Instagram captions.
Drafted a function-conversion tax memo in 30 minutes with AI — replaced a 50K EUR advisor quote, even covered GDPR.
Premium Co-Pilot filters the IBFD newsletter and surfaces only what's relevant. Drafted a memo for India — the local expert confirmed it was correct. Also generated a PowerPoint from it.
Used AI to draft constructive feedback on a colleague's presentation — peers praised the quality.
Built a 30-day study plan with AI as her trainer — daily readings + quizzes, AI decides when to go deeper.
Uses LocTax for complex tax setups globally — gives advice with IBFD references by jurisdiction. Claude takes a more risk-heavy approach; LocTax stays more neutral. Recommends it.
Used an AI agent to analyse a 2025 transfer-pricing court case — full answers + notices in 2 minutes once the company data was shared. Agent matures with every prompt.
Uses Co-Pilot to summarise his hundreds of daily email chains and pull out the key highlights.
Used AI to crunch complex financial computations.
Grok is linked to her Gmail, prior tax returns, payslips and passport. Voice-prompts country-specific returns; Grok scans, summarises, sends to the receiver — saves her half a day.
Voice translation at an NOB meeting (Dutch ↔ English) — phone records voice + translation so she can contribute live.
Used Claude to translate while travelling in Japan.
Co-Pilot's prompt function to capture argumental relationships and details during meetings.
Financial modelling with AI as a base — change a variable, AI adjusts the rest. Surprisingly accurate across markets.
Built one- and two-pager financial models from scratch via prompt, data pulled from Google. Change the tax rate and the agent adjusts entry/exit multiples automatically.
Ask AI for ERP t-codes to look up data fast instead of hunting through the system.
Built a ChatBot that takes user prompts, suggests t-codes, extracts data and builds dashboards for the centralised finance function in WorkDay.
Uses Slack to extract WorkDay ERP data — works for generic data, not salary fields.
PwC presented an AI that does SAP data extraction & analysis — figures out the output you'll need before you even specify the data requirements.
Uses Alteryx for data analysis and recognising patterns in tax data.
Used AI agents to file tax returns.

frustrations.text: I'd want AI to do the dishes at home
AI-generated Instagram captions aren't human enough.
Co-Pilot's answers can sometimes feel less analytical than expected.
LocTax is ~3,000 EUR / month for 5 users — a big investment for many tax teams.
If an agent does the technical advisory better, what is the in-house tax advisor's value-add now?
Communication stops feeling genuine when AI is replying to your colleagues on your behalf.
AI replies can sound superficial — people can tell it wasn't the in-house advisor speaking.
Leadership will blame the in-house practitioner if an AI mistake slips through unchecked.
AI calculations aren't always accurate, and the methodology can be questionable. It isn't always smart enough to compute the full thing.
Group IT calls to ask if we're "maxing out" the AI licence — and threatens to pull it if usage doesn't justify the cost. Feels intrusive.
Some companies won't even approve a 300 EUR AI budget for the tax team.
Co-Pilot's meeting capture invented "data" from a conversation that never happened — couldn't trust the output without re-reading it line by line.
AI-generated data-model formulas can quietly break.
Every call burns tokens. A human is still cheaper, and the KPIs don't always justify the data-centre cost.
Company cyber-security policies can throttle Co-Pilot/ChatGPT and reduce the analytical depth of the answers.

observations.text: Multinationals are looking to embed the IBFD database directly into their own systems instead of going through advisors.
Co-Pilot has different licences — the more your company pays, the more sophisticated the model.
We still need to learn to write very precise prompts to get good memos out of AI.
There could (and maybe should) be an audit standard for how AI is used in tax computation.
Some companies are starting to publish internal AI standards for responsible use.
Don't expect AI to be perfect — that's a bias we wouldn't apply to a human advisor. It's a tool, not an oracle.
Take small wins first — don't try to use AI in the most elaborate way from day one.
If AI is trained on human input, how will we keep advancing it once humans plateau?
Nothing wrong with criticising AI — disclaimers should be put on the output.
"We have to be human to use AI."
AI is developing fast — one day the mistakes it makes will be fewer than the ones humans make.
AI agents can train your talents — and your talents can train the agents — inside the organisation.
You can ask AI to write a prompt for you, then feed that prompt back in to get the best result.
